schema: MCT-COMBAT-DEEPEN-01 rule migration record, filled from original/templates_RULE_CHANGE.template.json
schema_extension_note: This document uses every field of the delivered RULE_CHANGE template. It ALSO carries one LOCAL extension, named legacy_tests, and states so explicitly: the migration index records that the original template has no field of that name, so it must not be presented as an original field. The extension exists because the delivery section asks for the retained old-behaviour checks to be listed with the retained entry point.
approved_scope: The delivered package's sixteen sub-orders and ninety-six acceptance cases, and nothing outside them. Every entry above is tied to a case or a design point of one of those orders; no rule, no vehicle and no parameter was changed because it seemed reasonable, and no unapproved expansion is claimed.
source_sha_note: Rule versions below are the versions this repository actually declares. No deployed version is invented, and rules that were verified rather than changed record the SAME version on both sides.
migration_index: WT-CD-007: family, pressure verdict, external flag, contact and world detonation, fragment candidates, expectation migration
WT-CD-008: versioned crew condition, and person identity separated from station and role
WT-CD-009: per-kind module response profile, and a breech failure judged once at a real request
WT-CD-010: an ammunition reaction profile by material, channel and compartment, with the legacy bustle rule kept
WT-CD-011: data declared per vehicle drive curves, and a bounded per vehicle recoil instead of one global kick
WT-CD-012: the observation, smoke and recon rules are confirmed in place and exercised by six scenes rather than replaced

evidence_state.claim: Everything recorded here belongs to the engineering self-consistent version. The delivered package contains no measured historical data, so no numeric agreement with War Thunder is claimed anywhere.
missing_references: real armour thickness and steel quality
range data for the delivered shells
material coefficients beyond the project design values

changes.reason: A finite round needs a declared sampled section rather than one centre line, so a grazing hit is decided by the round's width instead of by a coincidence of the aim line.
changes.legacy_entry: The v1 centre-line query is kept and used as the CONTROL in every shape case rather than replaced.
changes.new_expected_declared_before_run: With a declared section, none of the nine gap scenarios may disagree with the analytic gap geometry; the centre line alone disagreed on five of the nine.
changes.independent_oracle: Analytic slit geometry: a gap narrower than the round must block, wider than the round must pass.
changes.measured_before: v1 control: 5 of 9 scenarios disagree with the analytic geometry.
changes.measured_after: Declared section: 0 of 9 disagree.
changes.migration: A round without a declaration keeps the v1 centre line exactly. Records made under v1 keep v1 and are not recomputed.
changes.rollback: Remove the declaration; the v1 path is then the only path in use.
divergences: The sampled section is a project approximation; its error bound is declared in the profile, not measured.

changes.reason: Rotation was served as a step function: the part jumped to its end-of-step orientation and only its translation was interpolated, so a turning plate was met at the wrong time.
changes.legacy_entry: A part that does not turn still uses exactly one span and the previous basis behaviour, byte for byte.
changes.new_expected_declared_before_run: The rotating plate's crossing must match the analytic crossing within the chord bound of the declared angular step.
changes.independent_oracle: Bisection on the geometry alone: crossing fraction 0.537424 for a plate turning zero to forty five degrees against a fixed line.
changes.measured_before: Step function: crossing 0.583333, a delta of 0.045910, which is exactly what the end-of-step basis predicts.
changes.measured_after: Subdivided: crossing 0.536451, a delta of 0.000973; the frozen control is unchanged at 0.500000.
changes.migration: The subdivision is internal to a step; recorded results keep the version they were produced with.
changes.rollback: Set the angular step above any rotation, which restores the single-span path.
divergences: Two earlier attempts were disproved by measurement and are recorded in the CD003 evidence file.

changes.reason: One calibratable drag approximation is needed, and legacy rounds must use the old curve explicitly rather than have it silently changed.
changes.legacy_entry: v1_vacuum is the flight the project already had. An empty declaration resolves to it and is named legacy_v1_vacuum in the result.
changes.new_expected_declared_before_run: The declared retention curve must be the exponential e^(-k x) within its own tolerance of 0.010; the coefficient is calibrated from that curve rather than guessed.
changes.independent_oracle: Closed form under zero gravity, v(x) = v0 e^(-k x).
changes.measured_before: No profile existed; the flight was pure gravity.
changes.measured_after: Declared retention 0.972 / 0.932 / 0.869 / 0.811 against the frozen 0.972 / 0.932 / 0.871 / 0.814, worst deviation 0.0034; the vacuum control is bit-identical.
changes.migration: Rounds that declare nothing keep the vacuum curve. A record names the profile it flew with.
changes.rollback: Clear the declaration; the vacuum path returns.
divergences: The coefficient is a project design value awaiting human calibration and is labelled design, not validated_history.

changes.reason: The order asks for an explicit residual-velocity rule, and warns that the penetration budget is not joules: millimetres must not be pushed through a kinetic formula.
changes.legacy_entry: The rule is declaration gated. A round that does not ask for it keeps a speed scale of exactly one, which is the old behaviour.
legacy_tests: all fourteen suites, unchanged before and after
changes.new_expected_declared_before_run: A thicker plate must leave a lower residual speed, and the fuze must burst on that residual trajectory rather than on the pre-penetration speed.
changes.independent_oracle: A dimensionless mapping on consumed over available budget, declared with its constants; no energy conversion anywhere.
changes.measured_before: Penetration debited no speed at all: residual 900.000 after either plate.
changes.measured_after: One hundred millimetres leaves 805.788 and three hundred leaves 617.363; bursts land 19.11575 and 15.34726 metres out, inside one step of residual times delay.
changes.migration: Undeclared rounds are unchanged, so no saved result changes meaning. A record keeps the version it was fired under.
changes.rollback: Clear residual_model; the scale returns to one.
divergences: K and the floor are project design values, calibrated by declaration rather than against measured data.

changes.reason: The order requires the flight, the fire control and the AI prediction to share one solver rather than a copied parabola. Two predictors each held their own constant-acceleration copy and were blind to the drag.
changes.legacy_entry: With no drag declared the profile aware advance IS the constant acceleration advance, so every existing prediction is unchanged.
legacy_tests: run_ai_intercept_checks (106 passes, green through every step of this work)
changes.new_expected_declared_before_run: At the solver's own predicted time the flight's own method must reach the target within ten millimetres, with and without drag.
changes.independent_oracle: Two different code paths compared against each other: the solver's root finding against a step integration mirroring the manager's.
changes.measured_before: With drag declared the two integrations separated by 52.3367 metres in position and 100.7149 m/s in speed.
changes.measured_after: Vacuum miss 0.000305 m, unchanged; drag miss 0.001376 m, with the predicted time moved from 0.363637 s to 0.379341 s.
changes.migration: No stored prediction changes while no round declares a profile; a record names the rule version.
changes.rollback: Revert the commit; the two predictor copies return.
divergences: The refinement is an eight step bounded iteration with a forty step bisection inside; its convergence tolerance is declared in the code.

changes.reason: The order asks whether ERA is single use. It was verified rather than changed, so both sides name the same version and no deployed version is invented.
changes.legacy_entry: No behaviour was changed, so there is nothing to retain beyond the rule itself.
changes.new_expected_declared_before_run: The charge is spent only when its trigger conditions are met, and a second hit receives no un-consumed protection.
changes.independent_oracle: The rule's own declared trigger conditions, recomputed from the same inputs.
changes.measured_before: Not previously measured as a case.
changes.measured_after: A qualifying hit spends the charge and adds its reduction; a hit below the trigger minimum does NOT spend it; through the resolver a live charge costs 220.0000 mm against a spent charge's 100.0000 mm.
changes.migration: None needed: the rule is unchanged. A record names the reactive version whenever ERA events occurred.
changes.rollback: Not applicable to a verification with no change.

changes.reason: The content gate requires a family whose declared source type and effect agree with each other, and there was no family for an external blast, so one is added beside the existing four instead of relabelling an existing family.
changes.legacy_entry: The four existing families and every round admitted under them are untouched; a round that declares no family is still refused exactly as before.
changes.new_expected_declared_before_run: The engineering HE is admitted by the shell catalogue and offered at runtime by the vehicle carrying its gun and by no other.
changes.independent_oracle: The shell catalogue build result and the runtime option list per engineering vehicle, read from the production install path.
changes.measured_before: Measured: the shell catalogue REFUSED the round with "shell.<id>: effect_policy: unsupported", and the content pipeline likewise.
changes.measured_after: Measured: VehicleShellCatalog.build ok=true, and the runtime option list is three rounds on the vehicle carrying the 125 mm gun and two on the other, so the weapon limit holds at the configuration, admission and runtime layers.
changes.migration: A round without the declaration keeps the previous refusal word for word; records made before the family existed are not rewritten.
changes.rollback: Remove the family entry; the round is then refused by name exactly as it was before.
changes.divergences: The engineering round carries project design initial values only; no historical round or figure is claimed.

changes.reason: An external blast needs its own pressure verdict rather than a legacy fragment template, and that verdict must follow from bounded connectivity: pressure reaches the interior only through a breach or a declared opening, and never through a wall.
changes.legacy_entry: The internal burst and long rod profiles keep their own recorded versions and are not touched by this rule.
changes.legacy_tests: tests/probe_cd007_he_spec.gd (root event shape) and tests/probe_cd007_open_contrast.gd (open against closed)
changes.new_expected_declared_before_run: With the rule declared, a closed compartment with no breach and no declared opening must record the pressure as NOT applied, and an open one must record it as applied.
changes.independent_oracle: The declared layout openings carried in the query snapshot: the pressure verdict is decided by whether the burst is outside, whether the plate was breached, and how many declared open-fighting-compartment apertures the target has.
changes.measured_before: Measured: the burst carried only the legacy fragment template, with the blast channel marked applied=false and pending "cd07-blast-channel", so there was no pressure verdict at all.
changes.measured_after: Measured: the burst records three separate channels and the overpressure channel carries a computed verdict with the reason "closed compartment with no breach and no declared opening: the pressure has no path in, so there is no invented interior overpressure", while the open case records it as applied.
changes.migration: A burst that declares no external blast keeps the legacy template exactly; existing records keep the version they were made under.
changes.rollback: Remove the overpressure channel; the burst then carries the legacy template only, as before.
changes.divergences: The rule keys only on the open-fighting-compartment aperture because structural caps are the limit of inside travel rather than armour, so counting every aperture would make every vehicle look open.

changes.reason: Whether an explosion happened outside the hull is a property of every burst, not only of a fuzed one, and a contact HE carries no fuze at all.
changes.legacy_entry: Every fuzed burst keeps the same value it already recorded; nothing about the fuze path changes.
changes.new_expected_declared_before_run: A fuzeless external blast must record whether its explosion was outside the hull, rather than leaving the field absent.
changes.independent_oracle: The recorded external flag is compared against the burst geometry and the hull interior test.
changes.measured_before: Measured: a contact HE burst recorded the field as ABSENT, so nothing said whether it went off outside.
changes.measured_after: Measured: the same burst now records external=true, and the fuzed bursts are unchanged.
changes.migration: Bursts recorded before this change keep whatever they recorded; the field is added for new records only.
changes.rollback: Remove the unconditional write; fuzed bursts then record it as before and fuzeless ones record nothing.

changes.reason: The order requires contact HE and detonation after a world collision first, so an external blast bursts where it meets armour or the world instead of being stopped inert; proximity, timed and guided fuzes stay out of scope.
changes.legacy_entry: Every other effect keeps its behaviour exactly: the change is gated on the external blast policy alone, so internal burst, kinetic, long rod and chemical are untouched.
changes.new_expected_declared_before_run: With the rule declared, a round that meets armour and stops must still produce a root event, and a round that meets the world must produce one too.
changes.independent_oracle: The contact verdict the resolver returns, plus the recorded contact kind, so the two routes are distinguishable in the record.
changes.measured_before: Measured: the round met the armour with one contact and a stopped verdict and reported burst=none, so an external HE was inert on contact.
changes.measured_after: Measured: the same shot now reports burst=present with the three channels, the world route records contact_kind=world_contact, and the armour route is unchanged in every other respect.
changes.migration: A round that declares another effect is unaffected; the recording is additive and the terminal reason is still owned by the emitter.
changes.rollback: Remove the two gated branches; an external blast is then stopped inert again.
changes.divergences: The terminal reason for the world route is internal_burst because the emitter owns it; the contact kind therefore has to be recorded on the burst rather than inferred from the terminal name.

changes.reason: Five places in the fragment loop assumed a non-delayed effect happened inside its target, which is false for an external blast: it is inside none, has no burst target, and must still be able to act on any object its fragments reach while world occlusion still decides what they strike.
changes.legacy_entry: Delayed and spall fragments keep exactly the eligibility, guard, travel and target rules they had; every change is gated on the external blast policy.
changes.new_expected_declared_before_run: With the rule declared, a fragment from an external blast must be able to reach a target in range rather than stopping on the first iteration.
changes.independent_oracle: The occlusion contrast: a target behind an obstacle against one beside it at a reachable distance.
changes.measured_before: Measured: the loop treated an external blast as inside its (absent) target, so fragments exited on the first iteration or rejected every other target as other_target.
changes.measured_after: NOT YET MEASURED. The gated changes are in place but the occlusion contrast still records no damage on either target, so no positive effect is claimed; the remaining link is to be located by instrumenting the loop, which the recorded lessons require before further edits.
changes.migration: A round without the declaration keeps every one of the five behaviours exactly; the declaration only lifts them for this policy.
changes.rollback: Remove the five gates; the previous single-target assumption returns unchanged.
changes.divergences: This entry is deliberately recorded as necessary and NOT sufficient: it is kept because it corrects a real assumption, and it is explicitly not claimed to make external-blast fragments strike anything.

changes.reason: Adding a round type necessarily changes how a weapon distributes its rounds, because the install gives the default round seventy percent and splits the rest evenly; the shipping diagnostic asserted the old two-round total as a constant.
changes.legacy_entry: The historical two-round vehicles and their totals are unchanged; the assertion is satisfied by them as before.
changes.new_expected_declared_before_run: The battle must receive exactly the total the player edited, whatever number of round types the vehicle has.
changes.independent_oracle: The loadout the player edited: the sum of its own per-round counts.
changes.measured_before: Measured: the garage suite failed 27 of 29 with the constant, because the third round changed the distribution.
changes.measured_after: Measured: with the assertion expressed as the edited total the suite is 29 of 29, and the ten-suite run is 893 passes with no failures.
changes.migration: This is a migration of an expectation, not a relaxation: the constant asserted a number, the replacement asserts the invariant the leg was always about.
changes.rollback: Reinstate the constant; the two-round vehicles still satisfy it and a three-round one fails again.
changes.divergences: This is the only delivered expectation this order changed, and it changed because the order instructed adding a round, not to make a failure disappear.

changes.reason: Injury, station and availability must be three separate things, so a versioned condition replaces the boolean for reading while alive stays present and derived for anything that already reads it.
changes.legacy_entry: The legacy alive field is retained and derived, so a reader that only knows the boolean sees exactly what it saw before.
changes.new_expected_declared_before_run: With the condition declared, a graded state must exist as product state, and no middle condition may reduce duty because no efficiency figure has been verified.
changes.independent_oracle: The product produced crew state read before any submission, so a condition written by the test itself cannot be mistaken for the product.
changes.measured_before: Measured: the product crew record was {"alive":true,"original_role":...} only - a boolean, with nothing to grade.
changes.measured_after: Measured: every record carries condition, condition_version and severity, the scene reads met, and availability still only depends on incapacitation so no unconfirmed penalty is switched on.
changes.migration: A record without a condition falls back to the boolean; nothing that reads alive changes.
changes.rollback: Remove the condition fields; the boolean is then the only state again, as before.
changes.divergences: Thresholds are project design initial values and are declared as such; no external efficiency figure is claimed.

changes.reason: A person must be identifiable apart from the station they occupy, and a relief move must move the person rather than duplicate one; the training layout already had a station id and a role that differ, so the identity had to be separated from both.
changes.legacy_entry: The role remains the bridge between station and person, so every reader resolves a person through the assignments map exactly as before.
changes.legacy_tests: tests/run_damage_checks.gd, tests/run_recovery_checks.gd, tests/run_ammo_compartment_checks.gd, tests/run_recovery_player_checks.gd (the crew legs in each)
changes.new_expected_declared_before_run: With identities separated, no non-empty person holds two roles after a relief move, the headcount is conserved and the moving person keeps their own state and injuries.
changes.independent_oracle: The replacement path measured directly by a probe that builds its own actor: one empty slot, no duplicate, headcount unchanged.
changes.measured_before: Measured: a person key WAS the station key, so a person and a station were not distinguishable; the assignment map was keyed by role while station ids were read as persons.
changes.measured_after: Measured: person keys are person_1..person_N, station_roles keeps station to role, station_occupancy keeps station to person, the acceptance scene reads met, and thirteen suites return their exact baseline result counts with no runtime errors.
changes.migration: This one REQUIRED migrating delivered legs: seven sites named a person by a role or read a role as a person, and each was rewritten data driven - stronger than the name it replaced. The migration is recorded here as the class the package rule change section describes.
changes.rollback: Revert the identity assignment; a person is then the station again and the seven legs pass as before.
changes.divergences: A delivered test may still name a role where a person belongs; the eight such sites found are fixed, and the recovery player suite is window required under headless by design.

changes.reason: A module mattered only at exactly zero, so ability was all or nothing; the order requires a response chosen by KIND and forbids one uniform multiplier for every module.
changes.legacy_entry: Every strategy still reaches exactly zero at zero integrity, which is the behaviour the existing suites assert today, and the boolean that says whether the vehicle can move at all keeps its old meaning.
changes.legacy_tests: tests/run_damage_checks.gd and the six capability consumers, all unchanged
changes.new_expected_declared_before_run: With the profile declared, a partly damaged engine must reduce motive power before zero, and the tracks and barrel must behave as thresholds while the two turret axes stay linear.
changes.independent_oracle: The product produced capability dictionary read from the real state, with the new field carrying the curve.
changes.measured_before: Measured: any module above zero was skipped outright, so a half damaged engine left drive and steering exactly intact and recorded no reason at all.
changes.measured_after: Measured: an engine taken from full to half records power_scale 0.5 and the reason engine:linear:0.50, while a transmission loss, a track side loss and a driver loss record three different causes with different steering and pivot outcomes.
changes.migration: A module without a profile entry keeps binary-at-zero behaviour, which is what the delivery set mostly uses; the two axis drives keep the linear behaviour they already had.
changes.rollback: Remove the profile; every kind is then binary at zero again, exactly as before.
changes.divergences: Every threshold and chance is a declared project design initial value and the comparison state is NOT_COMPARED; no efficiency figure is claimed as external truth.

changes.reason: A breech could only fail by reaching zero, and there was no failure vocabulary at all; the order requires a failure judged once at the correct stage of a real fire request, never re-rolled per frame, with a frozen inventory rule.
changes.legacy_entry: At zero integrity the breech still disables firing exactly as before, through the same match branch; nothing else about a fire request changed.
changes.legacy_tests: tests/run_fire_control_checks.gd, tests/run_loading_checks.gd and every suite that fires, all unchanged
changes.new_expected_declared_before_run: With the rule declared, a real request against a damaged breech must be able to jam, the jam must be a committed record carrying a seed and a rule, the same request must answer the same way, and no round may be consumed.
changes.independent_oracle: The production request path itself: gunner.try_fire over a real actor, with the judgement rolled from the same deterministic seed the shot already uses.
changes.measured_before: Measured: the gunner blocked reasons were cooldown, grace, barrel occlusion, ammunition, capacity and malformed requests only - there was no breech or jam vocabulary anywhere.
changes.measured_after: Measured on the production path: after nine real requests a jam occurred and recorded {shot_id 9, seed 2335249131, roll 0.131, chance 0.2, rule cd009-breech-jam-v1, round_consumed false}; the same request was refused the same way; a held trigger did not multiply the record; and the magazine went 104 to 96 with the jam itself consuming nothing. The roll was also shown to be a pure function of the shot seed, with 20 of 80 sampled shots inside the declared chance.
changes.migration: A vehicle whose breech is undamaged never rolls at all, because the profile declares the kind probabilistic but the chance is scaled by the damage; the existing zero-integrity behaviour is untouched.
changes.rollback: Remove the judgement; the breech then only disables firing at zero, exactly as before.
changes.divergences: The chance is a declared project design initial value with comparison NOT_COMPARED, and the rule is frozen: a jam consumes no round and damages no component in this version.

changes.reason: A hit on stored ammunition only reported whether the contents were known, and the compartment rule that already existed was read by nothing, so an inert body store and a propellant store could not differ and a perforated partition changed nothing. The order forbids turning every rack at zero into a guaranteed detonation and forbids reading an inert penetrator as proof that no propellant risk exists.
changes.legacy_entry: AmmoCompartmentProfile, version wt015-rear-bustle-v1, is KEPT and remains reachable through the new profile as the legacy strategy; the Leopard bustle rule is not replaced and not deleted.
changes.new_expected_declared_before_run: With the profile declared, an inert body store and a propellant store must answer from their own material rules, an intact and a perforated compartment must differ, and the loss must leave the racks and appear in lost so the single ledger still balances.
changes.independent_oracle: The production inventory ledger itself: ready plus reserve plus in transfer plus chamber plus fired plus lost must account for what was supplied.
changes.measured_before: Measured: the ammunition branch of the damage resolver only produced ammo_contents_empty, there was no reaction profile at all (mentioned four times, implemented nowhere), and driving the Leopard partition to zero left the inventory total at forty two, which showed that nothing read the partition state.
changes.measured_after: Measured: the profile answers with one of four outcomes keyed on storage class, damage channel and compartment state; the fourth case reads isolated against vent_only once the real barrier module is the one damaged; and the conservation prints exactly - the T-80 accounts for 37 in racks plus 1 chambered against 38 supplied, the Leopard for 41 plus 1 against 42.
changes.migration: A vehicle whose store carries no declared protection policy is treated as mixed storage, which is the conservative reading; the legacy compartment rule is untouched and keeps its determinism.
changes.rollback: Remove the reaction call and the record; a hit on ammunition then reports only whether the contents are known, exactly as before.
changes.divergences: Every chance, loss fraction and isolation credit is a declared project design initial value with comparison NOT_COMPARED; no real ammunition behaviour is claimed, and where no dynamic door model exists the project keeps a logical abstraction with a scope note.

changes.reason: A per vehicle curve was hard coded per vehicle id in the content pipeline, so the two engineering vehicles shared one curve. The order requires each vehicle own frozen configuration to be visible in the result, and it forbids inventing historical gear ratios, so the curves are declared as project design values in each packet and read from data.
changes.legacy_entry: A packet that declares no drive profile still falls through to the hard coded per id design resource in the match, which is left untouched, so every existing vehicle behaves exactly as before.
changes.legacy_tests: tests/run_drive_checks.gd, run_slope_pivot_checks.gd, run_track_damage_checks.gd, run_surface_drive_checks.gd, run_track_drive_checks.gd, run_airborne_drive_checks.gd, all unchanged
changes.new_expected_declared_before_run: With the profiles declared, the two vehicles must differ in turn falloff, turn drag, track spacing, damaged track scale and power falloff, and the measured curve must follow each one.
changes.independent_oracle: The production content pipeline and the capability-free power train advance, read from the real vehicles admitted through the documented engineering entry point.
changes.measured_before: Measured: both vehicles returned the SAME forward top speed of 10.498 and the same reverse top of -2.778, with turn falloff 0.350 and track spacing 2.500 for both, because neither packet declared a curve and both fell through to one shared default.
changes.measured_after: Measured: the Leopard reads power falloff 0.500, six gears, turn falloff 0.420, track spacing 2.880 and turn drag 0.400 while the T-80 reads 0.420, five gears, 0.300, 2.720 and 0.320, and their forward tops differ at 10.304 against 10.373.
changes.migration: The allowed field table gained the drive profile names, and an explicit OPTIONAL set was added beside it so that listing a new name does not retroactively make it mandatory for every envelope already written - which is exactly what broke an in-memory packet in another suite before the set existed.
changes.rollback: Remove the drive_profile key from the two packets; both then fall through to the hard coded per id resource again, exactly as before.
changes.divergences: Every value is a declared project design initial value with comparison NOT_COMPARED; no historical gear ratio is invented and no real vehicle performance is claimed.

changes.reason: The recoil response read one global pair of constants, so every gun on every vehicle kicked the hull by the same amount, which the order forbids by name. The response must come from each vehicle own profile, be bounded and not accumulate.
changes.legacy_entry: Both new fields default to exactly the global constants the uniform kick already used, so a vehicle whose profile declares nothing keeps byte for byte the old behaviour. The damping stays global, because that is where the attenuation reads it.
changes.legacy_tests: tests/run_drive_checks.gd and every suite that fires, all unchanged
changes.new_expected_declared_before_run: With the profile declared, the recoil from the real entry must differ per vehicle, be capped, and not drift.
changes.independent_oracle: The real TankVehicle.kick_recoil entry, read from recoil_velocity before and after, on both engineering vehicles.
changes.measured_before: Measured: kick_recoil moved the hull by exactly the global constant 0.65 for both vehicles, which is one uniform kick and is what the order names as forbidden.
changes.measured_after: Measured: the Leopard moves 0.780 and the T-80 0.550 through the same entry, so the response differs by vehicle, and both are bounded by their own declared caps of 1.55 and 1.10.
changes.migration: A device fault was found and fixed on the way: the probe had been reading forward_speed while the recoil is applied to a separate recoil_velocity vector, which is why the first reading was zero for both vehicles and looked like a missing response rather than a wrong field.
changes.rollback: Clear the two values from the packets; both then read the global default of 0.65 again, exactly as before.
changes.divergences: Both values are declared project design initial values with comparison NOT_COMPARED; the order explicitly does not require realistic impulse figures and none are claimed.

changes.reason: The order asks for observation, sight intent, barrel ability and visible information to be SEPARATED, for ranging, zeroing, muzzle occlusion and the actual shot to share one solve, for an unequipped vehicle to be denied rather than given a fake sensor, and for smoke to affect both the player aids and the AI. The reading found the policy and support machinery already present and unwired, so this sub-order CONFIRMS and WIRES it rather than writing a second perception system, which the order forbids by name.
changes.legacy_entry: Every existing policy and support rule keeps its identity: INFO_CLASSES, PRECISION_M, MEDIA_RULES, INTERNAL_FIELDS, the per vehicle smoke and recon declarations, and the physical blocking rule are unchanged and remain the only authority.
changes.legacy_tests: tests/run_observation_policy_checks.gd 32/0, run_optics_checks.gd 24/0, run_sight_ballistics_checks.gd 73/0, run_support_actions_checks.gd 51/0, run_modern_support_checks.gd 19/0, run_partial_support_checks.gd 7/0, run_fire_control_checks.gd 59/0, all unchanged
changes.new_expected_declared_before_run: With the separation declared, an observation must not command the turret, the stabiliser must be a configured capability and not a camera option, a building must block a projectile while smoke must not, smoke must occlude the optical channel more than the thermal one, world truth must be refused from a client view, a recon mark must carry its source and expire, and an unequipped vehicle must report no smoke and no recon.
changes.independent_oracle: The policy and support objects themselves, read from the production classes rather than from a fixture that mimics them.
changes.measured_before: Measured by reading the sources rather than assumed: all six named files exist, the four information classes with their per source precision and expiry were already declared, smoke and recon were already declared per vehicle with a mark carrying source and expires_at, and the two engineering vehicles carried no optics profile while both the camera and the fire control already read one.
changes.measured_after: Measured by the six acceptance scenes: an observation leaves the turret yaw at zero rather than commanding it; the stabiliser reads false when absent and true when present; a building blocks a projectile while smoke does not, and smoke occludes the optical channel at 1.000 against 0.600 for thermal; world truth is refused from a client view with the reason world_truth_is_authority_only; a recon mark is created with one mark now and none after expiry; and the unequipped hull reports no smoke and no recon while an equipped vehicle reports both.
changes.migration: The rules are kept as they are and CONFIRMED rather than replaced, and the scenes exercise the production objects directly, so the wiring that remains is on the command and information interfaces rather than in the policy itself.
changes.rollback: No policy value was changed, so there is nothing to roll back in the rules; removing the scenes leaves the machinery exactly as it was found.
changes.divergences: Every precision, expiry, attenuation and blocking value remains a declared project design initial value with comparison NOT_COMPARED. Thermal and radar remain explicitly unsupported states rather than a grey filter standing in for a sensor, and no sensor ability is granted to a vehicle that does not carry it.

divergences.detail: The project config declares 50 mm / 2 percent while the reference packet declares 1 mm / 0.1 percent. Both are recorded; reconciliation needs the user.
Eleven registered items are model coverage rather than authored geometry; no layout fault was found and completion of the models would close them.
NOT_RUN. Fixtures do not substitute for a normal match and this agent does not sign for human play.
The declared effective range is 200 m, so the 500, 1000 and 1500 m rows of the sampling table are extrapolation only and carry no performance promise.
Not established: the package carries no measured historical data, so all values are project design initial values.

rollback_policy: Every change above is either declaration gated or confined to a code path that a declaration selects, so reverting the commit, or removing the declaration, restores the previous behaviour. Old records keep the version they were produced with and are never recomputed across versions.
